newsitem.title: POLAND: Dutch SHV to invest $100 mln in Poland in 1997. [CORRECTED 17:06 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dutch SHV to invest $100 mln in Poland in 1997. [CORRECTED 17:06 GMT]

text.p: Dutch group SHV Holdings NV plans to invest $100 million next year to expand its "Makro Cash and Carry" trading centre (corrects from hypermarket) network in Poland, the groups' Polish unit said on Thursday.

Wojciech Zipser, the spokesman for Makro Cash and Carry Poland sp. z o.o., told a news briefing that the company wanted to increase the number of its Polish stores up to 15 next year from 10 this year.
"Plans for 1997 envisage building four or five markets," Zipser said.
Makro, which has so far invested about $200 million in Poland, opened its ninth Polish hypermarket earlier this week and plans to launch one more by the end of the year.
The company will open a tender for the construction of the markets, Zipser said. Most of the previous tenders have been won by construction firms Budimex and Exbud.

Zipser also said the Dutch group's Polish unit would serve as an example in the company's expansion in other east European countries (corrects by clarifying that the Polish unit will not be used in the company's expansion).
